From 07704bbf36f57e4379e4cadf96410dab14621e3b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 16:05:54 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ALSA: fireworks: bound device-supplied status before string
 array lookup

The status field in an EFW response is a 32-bit value supplied by the
firewire device.  efr_status_names[] has 17 entries so a status value
outside that range goes off into the weeds when looking at the %s value.

Even worse, the status could return EFR_STATUS_INCOMPLETE which is
0x80000000, and is obviously not in that array of potential strings.

Fix this up by properly bounding the index against the array size and
printing "unknown" if it's not recognized.

Cc: Clemens Ladisch <clemens@ladisch.de>
Cc: Takashi Sakamoto <o-takashi@sakamocchi.jp>
Cc: Jaroslav Kysela <perex@perex.cz>
Cc: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.com>
Fixes: bde8a8f23bbe ("ALSA: fireworks: Add transaction and some commands")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Assisted-by: gregkh_clanker_t1000
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Reviewed-by: Takashi Sakamoto <o-takashi@sakamocchi.jp>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/2026040953-astute-camera-1aa1@gregkh
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

diff --git a/sound/firewire/fireworks/fireworks_command.c b/sound/firewire/fireworks/fireworks_command.c
index 2b595ee0bc35..05550f36fac5 100644
--- a/sound/firewire/fireworks/fireworks_command.c
+++ b/sound/firewire/fireworks/fireworks_command.c
@@ -151,10 +151,13 @@ efw_transaction(struct snd_efw *efw, unsigned int category,
 	    (be32_to_cpu(header->category) != category) ||
 	    (be32_to_cpu(header->command) != command) ||
 	    (be32_to_cpu(header->status) != EFR_STATUS_OK)) {
+		u32 st = be32_to_cpu(header->status);
+
 		dev_err(&efw->unit->device, "EFW command failed [%u/%u]: %s\n",
 			be32_to_cpu(header->category),
 			be32_to_cpu(header->command),
-			efr_status_names[be32_to_cpu(header->status)]);
+			st < ARRAY_SIZE(efr_status_names) ?
+				efr_status_names[st] : "unknown");
 		err = -EIO;
 		goto end;
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

The patch fixes an out-of-bounds memory access in the ALSA Fireworks driver. The bug occurs when a device-supplied status value from an EFW response is used directly as an index into the fixed-size `efr_status_names[]` array (17 entries). A status value outside 0–16, such as `EFR_STATUS_INCOMPLETE` (0x80000000), would cause an illegal array index read.

### Modifications in `sound/firewire/fireworks/fireworks_command.c`

- **Added a local variable** `u32 st` to store the decoded status value (`be32_to_cpu(header->status)`).
- **Changed the array lookup** from `efr_status_names[be32_to_cpu(header->status)]` to a conditional expression that checks whether the status value is less than `ARRAY_SIZE(efr_status_names)`.
  - If within bounds, the corresponding string from `efr_status_names[]` is printed.
  - If out of bounds (including negative values interpreted as unsigned), the literal `"unknown"` is printed instead.

### Relationships Between Changes

- The core fix is the bound check, which prevents an invalid array index. The local variable `st` makes the code clearer and avoids multiple conversions of the same value.
- The change ensures that all possible device-supplied status values are handled safely, eliminating the potential for out-of-bounds reads in the error logging path.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>dev_err(&efw->unit->device, "EFW command failed [%u/%u]: %s\n",
        be32_to_cpu(header->category),
        be32_to_cpu(header->command),
        efr_status_names[be32_to_cpu(header->status)]);</text>
Reason:
The status field (`header->status`) is a 32-bit value supplied by the firewire device. It is used directly as an index into the fixed-size array `efr_status_names[]` which has only 17 entries (indices 0–16). Without bounds checking, a status value outside this range (e.g., `EFR_STATUS_INCOMPLETE` = 0x80000000) causes an out-of-bounds array access, leading to undefined behavior or a crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>u32 st = be32_to_cpu(header->status);
dev_err(&efw->unit->device, "EFW command failed [%u/%u]: %s\n",
        be32_to_cpu(header->category),
        be32_to_cpu(header->command),
        st < ARRAY_SIZE(efr_status_names) ?
                efr_status_names[st] : "unknown");</text>
Reason:
The fix introduces a local variable `st` to hold the status value, then checks whether `st` is less than the number of elements in `efr_status_names` using `ARRAY_SIZE`. If the status is within the valid range, the corresponding string is used; otherwise, the string `"unknown"` is printed. This prevents any out-of-bounds array access and safely handles any unexpected status value from the device.
